beats.text: An old painter sold every color in his eyes to save his wife.
You see, in this city, colors are money.
There's a shop on every corner that'll pull a color right out of your eyes.
Sell green, and every tree you ever see turns gray.
Sell red, and roses look like ash.
The rich buy colors by the bucket.
Their side of the river glows like a candy store.
On the other side, everything looks like an old newspaper.
Parents there tell their kids what blue used to look like.
Arlo was a painter, so he never sold a single color.
And his favorite was yellow.
The color of his wife's raincoat.
The color of the sunflowers she planted every spring.
Then June got sick.
And her medicine costs one color a week.
So Arlo sells green.
Then blue.
Then red.
His paintings fade to gray, one by one.
Until there's only one color left.
Yellow.
And the old woman behind the counter takes off her glasses and says,
Son, after this, you'll never see her raincoat again.
He sells it anyway.
And it pays for everything.
A month later, June comes home, healthy, hiding something behind her back.
A tiny glass jar, glowing gold.
I bought your yellow back, she says.
Now you can paint my sunflowers again.
And for the first time in months, Arlo sees her raincoat shine.
Then he notices her squinting at the jar, like she can't tell what color it is.
She sold every color she had to buy his back.
Green. Blue. Red. And her yellow, too.
Every spring, she still plants sunflowers.
And he's the only one who can see them.
